title: Philipp Schmid 撰文解释为何在 Skills 与 CLI 兴起后仍更看好 MCP

report.summary: Philipp Schmid argues MCP is thriving despite the Skills and CLI backlash, citing millions of weekly agent actions at Linear, Notion and Atlassian, and four directions that will define it through 2027.
report.background: MCP (Model Context Protocol) has been through a full hype cycle in roughly 18 months: early enthusiasm, then a sharp backlash over context bloat, then a developer drift toward CLIs and progressive disclosure once Anthropic-style "Skills" arrived. The criticism was that dumping dozens of tool schemas into a prompt was wasteful when a shell command or a loadable skill file did the same job. Schmid argues that read of the market was wrong. The protocol itself kept improving — the 2026-07-28 spec removed stateful sessions, added an official extension system, and clients grew smarter about how to consume extensions. Meanwhile enterprise SaaS vendors such as Linear, Notion, Atlassian, Neon and even Apple (local MCP servers for Pages, Numbers and Keynote) shipped production servers, giving MCP something CLIs rarely have: measured, large-scale usage inside non-technical teams.
key_points: Real usage, not vibes: roughly half of Linear and Notion issues and pages (about 2.4 million per week) are now created by agents, Notion reports 60x MCP traffic growth, Atlassian handles over 5 million MCP tool calls per weekday, and 44% of Atlassian's users sit outside software teams — contexts where a CLI was never an option.

Code Mode replaces one-tool-per-turn calling: instead of stuffing 50 schemas into the prompt, the model gets a sandbox where MCP tools are typed functions. It writes one script that chains calls, filters and joins in cheap memory, and returns only the useful result — especially effective when servers declare outputSchema so clients can pre-generate typed stubs.

Skills move inside MCP: the io.modelcontextprotocol/skills extension exposes each skill as a skill:// URI with YAML frontmatter and SHA-256 file digests, so a harness injects only names and descriptions up front, pulls the full SKILL.md on demand, and auto-refreshes when a vendor updates a skill. Anthropic is already beta-testing Skills over MCP with Shopify, HubSpot and Atlassian.

MCP Events turn pull-only integrations push-capable: servers declare events and clients subscribe via webhook, long-lived stream or polling, each with cursors and eventId deduplication. That enables always-on, multi-human agents — a 2 a.m. P0 alert can wake an agent that triages before anyone opens their inbox. Early adopters include Shop MCP and Vercel.

MCP Apps and open gaps: servers can return sandboxed interactive HTML (dashboards, charts, design boards) rendered inline in Slack's new MCP client, Claude connectors and Google Antigravity. Schmid also flags unsolved issues: observability (servers see tool calls, not intent), discovery via scattered registries, and an expanded prompt-injection surface across webhooks, sandboxes and iframes.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this reframes the competition: the protocol layer is settling, so advantage shifts to harness quality and MCP client sophistication rather than custom multi-agent protocols. Schmid predicts the best 2027 agent harnesses will win on MCP integration — and will themselves expose an MCP server, letting sub-agents coordinate as MCP Tasks with Events waking the orchestrator. For developers, the practical checklist changes: declare outputSchema and structuredContent, support multimodal blocks in one call, use per-user OAuth 2.1 with fine-grained scopes instead of disk-stored API keys, and ship event subscriptions rather than requiring glue-code webhooks. For regular users, the payoff is less visible plumbing and more visible capability: agents that wake up on alerts, act on their behalf inside SaaS tools, and render interactive results in the chat window instead of raw JSON.
report.tools: Watch the Code Mode adopters — Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, OpenCode 2.0, Pi and Factory Droid — since they ship it as the default calling pattern. On the server side, study production MCP servers from Linear, Notion, Atlassian, Neon and Apple's local Pages/Numbers/Keynote servers. For the extensions, follow io.modelcontextprotocol/skills (Anthropic's Skills over MCP beta), io.modelcontextprotocol/events plus io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks, and io.modelcontextprotocol/ui for MCP Apps. Cloudflare's submit_feedback tool is a useful reference for the observability gap.
